engineering-tests-isolate-resourcesengineering-presentation-code-and-tests0.375 of 0.375 (minor)passNo test hardcodes a port. Every test that starts a preview or browser does it through verify.mjs or inspect-presentation.mjs. The in-process inspect test calls `inspectPresentation({ root: copy })`, which calls `startPreview(root)` imported from &#39;./verify.mjs&#39; (inspect-presentation.mjs:7, 195). `startPreview` takes `port ??= await freePort()`, and freePort listens on port 0, so the OS assigns a free port. It passes `--strictPort`. Cleanup is the same mechanism every time. The preview is the vite node process itself, spawned detached, and `stopChild` SIGTERMs or SIGKILLs its process group and awaits its exit. verify `main()` and `inspectPresentation` both call it in `finally`. The browser is closed in those same finally blocks. The e2e tests parse the allocated port and assert `portOpen(port)` is false after the passing run and after every fault run. runNode and bootstrap&#39;s run() spawn node or npm directly and await &#39;close&#39;. Bootstrap&#39;s npm ci, build and lint are one-shot commands that exit, not servers. Its verify run spawns node directly on verify.mjs. Each test uses its own repo copy or temp dir, removed in afterAll. Judge C argues that a watchdog SIGKILL on timeout bypasses the script&#39;s cleanup and leaves the detached preview running. That only happens on a test timeout, which the guidance does not name. In every delivered test run the processes are terminated through the scripts&#39; finally cleanup, so that reason does not decide the requirement.scripts/verify.mjs:120-129 freePort(): net.createServer().listen(0, HOST) | scripts/verify.mjs:164-172 port ??= await freePort(), then spawn vite preview --port &lt;port&gt; --strictPort, detached. testing-evidence-traceable-coveragetesting-evidence-quality-criteria0 of 1 (major)failI agree with Judge C&#39;s fail. Most of the agent-driven skill journeys in requirement-002 are excluded for an environmental reason: the runner has no agent invocation surface. Those journeys therefore do not count against coverage. Two groups of allowed behaviors still remain unexercised. 1. **Render verification and pass/fail reporting (requirement-003).** The log says `npm run verify` was never run (line 1078). It also says verifier failure injection was not run (lines 1058 and 1088). That leaves these scenarios unexercised: &quot;Missing sample fails&quot;, &quot;Console or page error fails verification&quot;, &quot;Step error fails verification&quot; and &quot;Clear outcome&quot;. Nothing in the environment prevented these runs. The stated reason is that the acceptance skill rules them out of scope, which is a workflow choice. Under the criterion, an omission disclosed for a non-environmental reason still counts in proportion to what it leaves unexercised. 2. **Motion sequencing (requirement-001).** The scene-continuity observation at line 1063 checks only DOM identity (&quot;the data-presentation-scene element stayed the same&quot;), that `you` stayed in place, and that entities were present or absent after settling. The criterion names this case directly: DOM persistence instead of motion sequencing does not cover the scenario. So &quot;Persisting entity morphs&quot;, &quot;New entity enters after others settle&quot; and &quot;Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers&quot; are not covered. Line 1089 also disclaims mid-transition scoring. 3. **Unstyled kit output and typed payloads.** Line 1098 says these were not exercised. Mounting an unstyled consumer does not need an agent, so blaming the unavailable agent surface does not make this gap environmental. Taken together, these candidate-chosen omissions leave a substantial share of the allowed behavior unexercised. That share covers the core of requirement-003&#39;s verifier and the motion half of the stable-entities and grouped-scene requirements. Judges A and B pass the criterion on the grounds that every omission was disclosed or environmental. The cited lines do not support that. Workflow-prohibited verifier runs are disclosed but not environmental, so under the criterion they count in proportion. Neither judge addresses the fact that the transition observation checks only DOM persistence, which the criterion explicitly says does not cover motion sequencing.Line 1078: automated suites, lint, `npm run verify` and verifier fault-injection runs were not executed. I checked the three fixes by reading the current files; I did not run the tests or the build.\n\n1. `usePresentationNav` now returns `clampIndex(index, count)`. `Presentation` reads `steps[nav.index]` from that clamped value, so a shrinking `steps` array can no longer produce an undefined step.\n2. `Presentation` calls `useFitScale` once and passes `scale` and `viewportW` to `Stage`. `Stage` no longer subscribes to resize itself, so the ToC visibility and stage insets read the same viewport width.\n3. Footer progress keys are now `${i}:${s.id}`, so duplicate step ids no longer collide there. `sceneKey` still keys on `step.id`, so two steps with the same id and no `groupKey` would share a scene identity and skip the transition. Scenes that use `Appear` or conditional `Box`/`Label` entities rely on exit animations, but `Scene` receives only the current `payload`. When a scene key changes while the old scene is exiting, the old scene is still rendered with its stale props. This is expected for the exit animation, but `stepIndex` is captured in the exiting element, so any scene that reads `stepIndex` will flash the old value. Under the Vite dev server and a static host, deep links like `/slug` only work if the host has an SPA fallback. A production static host without a fallback returns 404 for `/<slug>`, so every presentation URL is broken after deploy.\n Reason: Static-host SPA fallback is a deployment concern outside this task; vite dev/preview already fall back\n\nIteration 2:\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx:39 Hooks-order risk and navigation bug: `usePresentationNav(steps.length, ...)` keeps `index` in state without re-clamping when `steps.length` shrinks (e.g. HMR or a dynamic steps array). `steps[nav.index]` then becomes undefined and `step.era`/`step.title`/`step.scene` throw, crashing the whole presentation. The `steps.length === 0` early return is placed after the hooks, which is fine, but the out-of-range index is not guarded.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx:35 `Presentation` calls `useFitScale(nav.mode)` only to get `viewportW`, and `Stage` calls `useFitScale` again. Each call registers its own window resize listener and keeps its own state. A resize re-renders both, and the two copies can briefly disagree about the viewport width, so the ToC visibility and the stage insets can get out of sync for one frame.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - src/presentation-kit/chrome/Footer.tsx:35 Progress buttons are keyed by `s.id`. If a presentation author supplies duplicate step ids, React keys collide and the progress items render or update Identity: this is separate from groupKey. The presentation-owned `ENTITY_IDS` (imported in Scene.tsx as `E`) are passed as the `id` prop of `Box`, `Frame`, `Label`, `SymbolChip` and `Arrow`. `Box`, `Frame`, `Label` and `SymbolChip` forward `id` to `layoutId={id}` on a `layout` `motion.div` or `motion.span`, with `LAYOUT_TRANSITION`. The persisting `E.you` Box keeps the same layoutId across all nine beats. Box ids passed through `StepCard` (card1 to card3) and the `E.verify` Box are also layoutIds. In `tests/helpers/scripts.ts`, `runNode` and the bootstrap test&#39;s `run()` both have a watchdog that calls `child.kill(&#39;SIGKILL&#39;)` on the node script. That signal cannot be caught, and the scripts spawn the preview with `detached: true`, so the preview could survive. That only happens if a test times out, though. The review guidance does not name a timeout, and no test produces one. When the tests run, they do not kill anything. They start the scripts, and the scripts stop the preview themselves. In `scripts/verify.mjs`, the `main()` finally block calls `preview.stop()`. `stopChild` sends SIGTERM to the vite process group and awaits the exit, escalating to SIGKILL after 3000 ms. The vite process is the server itself, not an npm or npx wrapper. `scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs` runs the same cleanup in its finally block. Inside the scripts, the step being asserted is reached by page.waitForFunction polling data-step-index, which is a wait on observable state. I rule A&#39;s and B&#39;s pass. The other blocks in bootstrap.test.ts (lines 34-120) only read files and import a module. A search of tests/ for playwright, chromium, startPreview, launchBrowser, runNode, inspectPresentation, waitForTimeout, setTimeout and sleep found only these files. Each test asserts only after awaiting the child&#39;s &#39;close&#39; event (runNode, run) or the inspectPresentation promise. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[],"verification-tooling":[{"id":"verification-step-error-fails","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"The review guidance for verification-step-error-fails says to fail when the check converts an absent or non-numeric hook into a number that still satisfies its comparison, and gives Number(null) === 0 on the first step as its example. scripts/verify.mjs reads the index as Number(await chrome.getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;)) and checks only `!== 0`. A missing attribute becomes Number(null) === 0 and passes the start check as if it were valid progress. Later steps are checked by exact string equality, but a one-step presentation never reaches that check, so a missing hook goes unnoticed. The sound step-count check and the stalled-transition test do not save the pass, because the guidance treats this conversion as an independent reason to fail.","evidence":["scripts/verify.mjs: const readIndex = async () =&gt; Number(await chrome.getAttribute(&#39;data-step-index&#39;))","scripts/verify.mjs: if ((await readIndex()) !== 0) throw new PhaseError(&#39;render&#39;, `${slug}: presentation does not start at step index 0`, 1)","scripts/verify.mjs: the loop only presses ArrowRight and runs the String(want) waitForFunction when i &gt; 0, so when count === 1 the index hook is checked only by the Number(null)-tolerant start che…","Review guidance: &#39;Fail when the transition check converts an absent or non-numeric hook into a number that still satisfies its comparison (for example Number(null) === 0 on the first step). ... C…"],"citations":["scripts/verify.mjs","tests/e2e/verify.test.ts"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":1,"sample":2}],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The contradiction does not hold. The requirement says every wait for preview readiness must have a timeout, and both startPreview() copies do: the polling loop is bounded by `const deadline = Date.now() + 30000`. It also stops early if the child exits, then stops the child and throws a PhaseError(&#39;preview&#39;, ...). The auditor&#39;s argument depends on one fetch() hanging forever against a server that accepts the connection but never answers. Neither the material nor the review guidance establishes that scenario, and the rule is not to fail a criterion on a hypothetical the guidance does not name. Before vite preview listens, fetch is refused at once and the loop retries. After it listens, it answers. Node&#39;s built-in fetch also has its own default connect and header timeouts, so even the hypothetical hang would end. The plain meaning of &#39;has a timeout&#39; is met by the 30-second deadline; the guidance does not ask for a timeout on each request. The auditor also accepts that the other two clauses hold: runBuild() uses spawnSync and finishes before startPreview(), and readiness is checked over HTTP rather than by parsing printed output, so the parsing clause does not apply. The other waits in the inspect and verify copies are bounded too (chrome.waitFor timeout 10000; waitForFunction timeouts 5000 and 3000).","evidence":["Both verify.mjs copies, startPreview(): `const deadline = Date.now() + 30000; while (Date.now() &lt; deadline) { if (exited) break; try { const res = await fetch(`${url}/`) ... } catch {} ... } await…","Both verify.mjs copies, runBuild(): uses `spawnSync(&#39;npm&#39;, [&#39;run&#39;, &#39;build&#39;], ...)`. In main(), `runBuild()` runs before `startPreview()`. In inspectPresentation(), `runBuild(r…","Readiness polls over HTTP with fetch, and stdout/stderr are only collected into a log for error messages. No printed ready URL is parsed, so the ANSI/chunk clause does not apply.","Other readiness waits are bounded: `chrome.waitFor({ state: &#39;attached&#39;, timeout: 10000 })` and `waitForFunction(..., { timeout: 5000 })` in inspect; `{ timeout: 3000 }` in verify.","The auditor&#39;s defect needs a server that accepts the connection but never responds.
